nodes.name: Carburization under reductive atmosphere
nodes.procedure: A series of samples including Mo2C, MoL-Mo2C, Pt1-Mo2C SACs, and Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs (with Pt loading of 1 wt.%) were synthesized via modified carburization process. MoL-Mo2C and Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs featuring metallic Mo nanolayer (MoL) were synthesized by carburizing the precursors under 1% H2/Ar atmosphere at 850°C. Under these conditions, diluted H2 selectively reduces the surface of Mo2C leading to partial surface reduction. Pt participates in Mo-NH2 complexation during synthesis of Pt-MoOx precursor, stabilizing Pt atoms during high-temperature carburization.

nodes.source_text: A series of samples, Mo2C, MoL-Mo2C, Pt1-Mo2C SACs, and Pt1-Mo2C SSAs (with a Pt loading of 1wt.%) , were synthesized via a modified carburization and re-carburization process (Figure 1a). MoL-Mo2C and Pt1-MoL-Mo2C SSAAs, featuring a metallic Mo nanolayer (MoL), were synthesized by carburizing the precursors under a 1% H2/Ar atmosphere at 850°C

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface areas from BET method: Pt₁-MoL-Mo₂C = 68.4±1.3 m²g⁻¹, Pt₁-Mo₂C = 65.1±1.1 m²g⁻¹, MoL-Mo₂C = 42.5±0.7 m²g⁻¹, Mo₂C = 39.1±0.8 m²g⁻¹ (Table 1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The BET surface areas of Pt₁-MoL-Mo₂C SSAAs and Pt₁-Mo₂C SACs are 68.4 and 65.1 m²g⁻¹, respectively, higher than those of MoL-Mo₂C (42.5 m²g⁻¹) and Mo₂C (39.1 m²g⁻¹), indicating that Pt incorporation induces a more open structure (Table 1).

nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt₁-MoL-Mo₂C SSAAs exhibit a major peak at 2.28 Å, corresponding to the Pt-Mo bond, which closely resembles the Mo-Mo bond length in metallic Mo foil (≈2.30 Å) ... the major peak at 2.45 Å is found for Pt₁-Mo₂C SACs, assigned to the Pt-Mo bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo-O stretching vibration at ≈1004 cm⁻¹ from adsorbed H₂O appears spontaneously on MoL-containing catalysts (Pt₁-MoL-Mo₂C, MoL-Mo₂C) even at open circuit.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt₁-MoL-Mo₂C SSAAs exhibit a broad peak at ≈1004 cm⁻¹, which corresponds to the characteristic stretching vibration of the Mo-O bond, where O originates from adsorbed H₂O molecules. Notably, this Mo-O vibrational peak appears even when no voltage is applied.
